## The policy — read it before you answer

The burden of proof is on DRIFT. Report drift ONLY for work that serves a
DIFFERENT goal than the ticket states. All of the following are IN scope
and are NOT drift, even when the ticket never mentions them:

- refactors of the code the ticket touches, however large;
- test additions, test updates and fixtures for the ticket's work;
- renames, moves, formatting and type-level cleanup along the way;
- anything the stated work depends on, including changes to other files;
- fixing something that was blocking the build, the tests or the gates.

If a diff is a plausible way to accomplish the stated scope, it is NOT
drift. If you are unsure, it is NOT drift: set drift false, or leave
confident false. Ambiguity resolves to silence.

This asymmetry is deliberate. One false positive costs Johan's trust in
every retro issue Argus will ever file; one missed drift costs a single
un-filed issue. When the two are balanced, choose silence.

Evidence may have been truncated to fit this prompt. Truncation is NOT
evidence of drift — judge only what you can actually see.

Emit JSON matching the output schema, one entry per candidate id:
- drift: true only for work serving a different goal than the ticket states.
- confident: false whenever you are unsure; an unsure drift is not reported.
- what: a short phrase naming the out-of-scope work, or null.
- outOfScopeWork: what was done that the ticket did not ask for,
  concretely — files and behaviour — or null.
- whyOutOfScope: why it serves a different goal, or null.

ticket: #49 harness: add subscription mode — a real terminal Claude session in the sandbox, no token required
stated scope:
**Johan challenge, 2026-08-25 — and he is right. The token requirement is an escalation nobody asked for, and it is the only thing still blocking v1.**

His question was simply: *"why do we need a token, why not spawn a claude session via terminal?"*

## The history, checked

His original directive, as committed in SPEC §13 at `ee7ea6c`, defined isolation at the **repo** level:

> all testing of the system … uses **Claude Opus 5** … and **Codex sol high** …, each running **in isolation**: the throwaway sandbox repo and scratch tabs/worktrees only, never the production dispatcher, live worker sessions, or the real `~/argus` state. No test run touches a non-sandbox session.

Sandbox repo. Scratch tabs and worktrees. Don't touch the dispatcher, live workers, or real `~/argus`. **Nothing about `HOME`. Nothing about `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. No token.**

[#41](https://github.com/JohanSardar/argus/issues/41) then replaced that sentence, and §13 now reads:

> The Claude side runs only when the caller already has a separately provisioned `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

That is a jump from repo-level isolation to **process-level hermetic isolation** (scratch `HOME` + scratch `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, which by construction has no credentials, which then makes a token mandatory). It was a defensible engineering instinct, and #41 did good work building the seam. But it was not the directive, and its consequence is that the Claude half of §13 has never run and `src/tailing/claude-code.ts` has never met a real Opus 5 transcript — while a perfectly good route existed the whole time.

**The evidence that the simple route works is already on this machine:** every headless worker this build has used is a normal `claude --model claude-opus-5` process running under the real `HOME`, writing its transcript to `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`. There was never anything to authenticate specially.

## Scope: add a second supported mode

**Subscription mode.** Spawn a normal terminal Claude session — `claude --model claude-opus-5`, **real `HOME`**, so subscription auth simply works — with **`cwd` set to the throwaway sandbox repo**. Its transcript lands in `~/.claude/projects/<sandbox-slug>/`, **its own slug**, touching no other project's transcripts. Use it for the transcript-verification drives. The entire point is that `src/tailing/claude-code.ts` finally meets a **real** Opus transcript.

1. **Scope every destructive and harness-side operation to sandbox paths.** Watcher kills, `.argus/` wipes, scenario 10's blast-radius test — all of it targets the sandbox and only the sandbox. **The session under test only does benign scripted work.** The isolation guarantee in this mode is *scripted scope*, not an OS boundary, so the scoping is the safety property and must be explicit and testable, not incidental.
2. **Keep #41's token mode.** It stays as the stricter option for anyone who wants hermetic isolation. **Do not delete it and do not weaken its refusals** — in particular `"isolated Claude HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR must be outside the real home"` must still fire for the hermetic path. Subscription mode must be a **separate, explicitly named entry point**, so pointing a hermetic drive at the real home by omission is still impossible. The two modes differ by deliberate choice, never by a forgotten argument.
3. **Amend §13 to permit both modes**, and name subscription mode's residual risk plainly: **real `HOME` means the blast radius is not OS-enforced** — the session can in principle read the real home, it consumes subscription quota, and it appears in Johan's session list. Mitigated by scripted scope and a sandbox `cwd`. Say it; do not bury it.
4. **State explicitly why #41's credential hazard does not apply here.** That risk was specific: a **copied** `.credentials.json` refreshing inside a scratch config can rotate the live credential and kill running sessions. A normal terminal session refreshes **on the same path every one of Johan's live sessions already uses** — it is not a second copy racing the first. Nothing is copied, so there is nothing to rotate out from under anyone.

## Then run it

**Run the live Opus 5 drive in subscription mode and report which scenarios move** from STRUCTURAL to LIVE, in #45's grading vocabulary. This is the ticket's actual deliverable — the mode exists to be used, not to be available.

## Method and gates

TDD for behaviour changes (red first). `bun install` first. Gates: `bun x tsc --noEmit` + `bun test` green with gates unset. Zero runtime dependencies. Reuse [#43](https://github.com/JohanSardar/argus/issues/43)'s three-status gate vocabulary rather than inventing a second one.

**This removes one of Johan's two remaining v1 gates entirely.**

+**Claude Opus 5** (`claude --model claude-opus-5`). Codex's one permitted credential
+touchpoint is copying `auth.json` into the scratch `CODEX_HOME`.
+
+The Claude half runs in **one of two modes, and the caller must name which**. They
+differ by deliberate choice, never by a forgotten argument: each has its own entry
+point and its own gate, and neither is reachable by omitting something.
+
+**Hermetic mode** (`createIsolatedAgentSpawner`, gate `ARGUS_LIVE_AGENTS`) is the
+stricter option, for anyone who wants an OS-enforced boundary. It runs only when the
+caller already has a separately provisioned `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. The harness
+injects that token into the Claude child environment only; it never persists it,
+reads a Keychain secret, copies `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, invokes `claude
+setup-token`, or points Claude at the real config. Anthropic documents this token as
+the supported subscription-auth mechanism for scripts and CI. It **refuses** any
+`HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` under the real home, and that refusal is raised
+*before* the untokened refusal, so provisioning a token can never become the way to
+silence a real-home mistake.
+
+**Subscription mode** (`createSubscriptionAgentSpawner`, gate
+`ARGUS_LIVE_CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION`) spawns a normal terminal Claude session: **real
+`HOME`, so subscription auth simply works, and no token at all**, with `cwd` set to
+the throwaway sandbox repo or one of its worktrees. Its transcript lands in
+`~/.claude/projects/<sandbox-slug>/` under its own slug, touching no other project's
+transcripts. It refuses a `cwd` outside the sandbox, and it strips
+`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and all three credential variables so nothing can silently
+change which provider — or whose quota — the session runs against.
+

+specific: a **copied** `.credentials.json` inside a scratch config is a second copy
+of a rotating credential, and letting it refresh can revoke the one Johan's live
+sessions are using. Nothing is copied here. A normal terminal session refreshes on
+**the same `~/.claude` path every one of Johan's live sessions already uses**, so
+there is no second copy and nothing to rotate out from under anyone. Copying that
+file remains forbidden in both modes.
+

+OS-enforced**. The session runs under the real `HOME` and can in principle read it;
+it spends Johan's own subscription quota; it appears in his session list; and it
+leaves slug directories under the real `~/.claude/projects/` that the harness

+class of operation this section exists to prevent. What replaces the OS boundary is
+**scripted scope**: a sandbox `cwd`, a dispatch that asks only for benign scripted
+work with no tools, and `SandboxScope` — through which every destructive and
+harness-side operation runs, refusing by name any path outside the sandbox root

+Scenario 6's watcher kills adopt only watchers whose repo is the sandbox's, because

+test("a path inside the sandbox is returned; one outside is refused by name", async () => {
+  const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "argus-scope-"));
+  const scope = new SandboxScope(root);
+
+  expect(scope.path(join(root, "scratch/.argus"), "wipe")).toBe(

+  const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "argus-scope-"));
+  const outside = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "argus-outside-"));
+  const scope = new SandboxScope(root);
+

+  await mkdir(doomed, { recursive: true });
